notes: Tristan da Cunha has no airport and no scheduled commercial air service, so airports is empty.

Access is only by ship, typically about 6 days each way from Cape Town, South Africa (CPT). Departures are infrequent, and a few fishing and supply vessels and some expedition cruises also call. Landing depends on weather and permission from the island administration. Visitors need advance approval, and berths are limited.

From DEN, fly to Cape Town (CPT), usually via a hub such as Johannesburg, London, or Doha. Then take a ship from Cape Town. Saint Helena (HLE) has flights from Johannesburg, but no ship links it to Tristan da Cunha on a regular schedule.
Daily cost is an estimate. The island uses the British pound, and food and lodging are mostly arranged through homestays. Ship passage is a separate and substantial cost.
The State Department advisory may be listed under a different name or grouped with the UK. Please verify.
Assumption for 'Tristan da Cunha': Interpreted as the island's only settlement, Edinburgh of the Seven Seas. The island has no airport.
